Job: Restore and validate directed tour-prerequisite storage and its reader on the prod-based auto-50-perc-off delivery branch, reusing compatible historical implementation and tests. Given a checkout tour ID and configured directed relationships, return whether the tour is configured and its prerequisite-tour IDs, supporting multiple prerequisites for later qualification through a paid purchase at any one of them. Keep source inspection, file-access checks, isolated branch setup and dependency adaptations within this job, preserving the other branch and its untracked work.

Why it matters: The assessed delivery baseline lacks this owner-required capability. Restoring it supplies the configuration boundary needed for the automatic 50% discount, with a bounded interface and historical reuse evidence. The snapshot establishes no blocker requiring a separate prerequisite job; executable compatibility belongs within restoration validation.

Done when: The resulting version and diff are retained, and the actual restored migration and reader execute against current dependencies in an isolated database, demonstrating configured-tour lookup, multiple prerequisites, unconfigured-tour behavior, relationship direction and isolated rollback, while preserving existing tours and rows. Target MySQL schema compatibility is inspected, with inspection distinguished from actual MySQL execution and unresolved database limitations recorded explicitly. A compatibility failure that prevents the capability from working means restoration is incomplete. Existing checkout, search, recognition, pricing and payment behavior remains unchanged; qualification, code selection, checkout integration, production configuration and deployment remain later work.
selection.selection_reasoning:
Recommend one bounded implementation atom: restore and validate directed tour-prerequisite storage and its reader on the owner-selected prod-based auto-50-perc-off delivery branch, reusing the historical implementation where compatible.

The fixed objective is the automatic 50% checkout discount. This atom would supply one necessary product capability: given a checkout tour ID, return whether that tour is configured for the discount and its directed prerequisite-tour IDs. Its expected contribution is removal of a demonstrated upstream implementation gap, not delivery of the discount itself.

Evidence supporting the choice

The latest assessment inspected committed tree 45826e12cdc8f585e514d7bb09c0d37fa28ed568 and found no matching prerequisite migration/service or prerequisite configuration identifiers in the searched customer web scope (E0995–E0997). Historical evidence reports a directed relationship migration and reader passing five isolated SQLite cases. The assessment identifies preserved source/tests and a concrete restoration boundary (E1023–E1045). Together, these establish a required missing capability and a credible bounded reuse route. They do not establish current executable compatibility: the assessment ran zero fresh product tests, and the active worktree remained on another branch.

Plausible alternatives

1. Restore the applicable existing 50% code selector. This directly supplies another missing delivery capability: deterministic selection of an applicable code or none. Historical evidence is substantial—19 cases and 25 input executions, including verification and usage-guard checks—and current ProductDiscount and supplied-code checkout surfaces provide integration targets. It can be developed independently of prerequisite storage. However, it would still leave the checkout without its configured eligibility boundary or paid-prerequisite qualification. Prerequisite restoration has a more explicitly specified current-baseline interface and acceptance boundary, with less interaction with existing pricing and code-use behavior. That makes it the better next bounded contribution, although selector restoration remains a strong subsequent option.

2. Run a focused recognition-to-paid-purchase compatibility experiment. Freeze representative cases and exercise existing recognition identifiers through historical evidence-resolution logic and current order/payment models. The observable result would be a supported association path—or a precise mismatch—for paid purchase evidence, including rejection of purchase-history entries without payment and handling of missing references. This addresses the most consequential semantic uncertainty: recognition matches alone do not prove the same person's paid prerequisite purchase. It could prevent later integration rework and does not depend on a completed prerequisite reader. Nevertheless, the snapshot supplies no evidence that resolving this uncertainty would eliminate or materially redesign the owner-required directed prerequisite relationship. The selected atom can therefore make necessary implementation progress while that uncertainty remains. An observed identifier incompatibility that threatens the existing recognition approach would strengthen the experiment's priority in a later selection.

A separate prerequisite compatibility-only investigation is better incorporated into the restoration atom's initial validation than selected as another research deliverable. Compatibility is unknown, not known to be broken. Repeating the completed baseline assessment would add little. New orchestration infrastructure lacks evidence of an unmet capability: the recorded installed builder already accepts bounded atoms and owns implementation, experiments and validation.

Selected atom boundary

Inputs: checkout tour ID and configured directed checkout-tour/prerequisite-tour pairs. Outputs: configuration status and prerequisite-tour IDs. Preserve multiple prerequisite relationships so later qualification can accept a paid purchase at any one of them; do not encode an all-prerequisites requirement or a single-row limit.

Scope: the additive relationship migration, reader, minimal adaptations needed for current dependencies, and focused validation. Preserve existing tours and rows. Checkout wiring, recognition policy, pricing, payment behavior, automatic code selection, production configuration and deployment remain outside this atom. These exclusions keep the contribution independently assessable; they do not reduce the final delivery requirements.

Execution prerequisites: establish an isolated working state for the already-selected delivery branch, identify the exact source version, access the preserved historical source/test bodies, and use current product dependencies with an isolated test database. The other active branch and its untracked work must be preserved. These are execution setup requirements, not reasons to reopen the owner's baseline decision or withhold this recommendation.

Completion evidence: retain the resulting version and diff; execute the actual restored migration and reader against current dependencies; demonstrate configured-tour lookup, multiple prerequisites, unconfigured-tour behavior, relationship direction and isolated rollback; and show existing tours/rows remain unchanged. Inspect target MySQL schema compatibility, clearly distinguishing inspection from actual MySQL execution. Historical SQLite results alone cannot establish MySQL readiness. Record any unresolved database limitation explicitly before migration deployment. If compatibility prevents completing this bounded capability, report the concrete failure rather than claiming successful restoration or silently expanding scope.

Why now

This choice converts the latest research into a necessary, testable product capability using existing building machinery and historical work. Priority follows from its explicit owner requirement, demonstrated baseline absence, clear interface and contained behavioral impact—not merely its position first in the checkout sequence. Recognition work and selector work can proceed independently; they are alternatives, not falsely blocked dependencies.

No missing analytical perspective prevents this comparison. Compatibility results belong to the proposed work. Live code availability, deployment behavior and kiosk scope remain relevant to later integration and delivery validation. The selected atom would demonstrate prerequisite storage and lookup only; the complete recognition-to-paid-purchase-to-discounted-order sequence before payment would remain unfinished. This is a recommendation, with no execution performed.
